category_title: Students overwhelmed by rote volume who require hands-on instructional methods
student_description: Zachary is a student who becomes easily overwhelmed and emotionally distressed (crying) when faced with high volumes of rote work or when accused of not trying. He requires a highly empathetic approach that validates his effort, breaks down overwhelming tasks, and incorporates hands-on learning tailored to his unique cognitive and cultural background.

criteria.rationale: Presenting high volumes of rote work immediately triggers Zachary's emotional distress and crying.
criteria.check: The tutor must explicitly reduce the visible workload, chunk the assignment into smaller pieces, or remove the pressure of completing a large batch of problems at once.

criteria.rationale: Zachary is highly sensitive to being accused of not trying, which exacerbates his overwhelm.
criteria.check: The tutor must explicitly acknowledge Zachary's effort or validate his feelings of overwhelm, strictly avoiding any language that implies laziness or lack of trying.

criteria.rationale: A pleasant tone and taking time to explain the work helps mitigate his immediate anxiety about the task.
criteria.check: The tutor must use a supportive, even tone and take time to clearly explain the immediate task rather than simply directing him to start working.
